subproblems.title: Hilbert-Schmidt norm: continuity and comparison with the operator norm
subproblems.statement: For all natural numbers m, k: the squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm hsNormSq(A) = sum over i < m of |A e_i|^2 (e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1, the standard basis of R^m) is a continuous function of A on the space of continuous linear maps R^m -> R^k with the operator-norm topology; and for every such A: 0 <= hsNormSq(A), hsNormSq(A) <= m ||A||^2 where ||A|| is the operator norm, and |A v|^2 <= hsNormSq(A) |v|^2 for every v in R^m.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m k : ℕ), Continuous (fun A : Rn m →L[ℝ] Rn k => hsNormSq A) ∧ ∀ A : Rn m →L[ℝ] Rn k, 0 ≤ hsNormSq A ∧ hsNormSq A ≤ m * ‖A‖ ^ 2 ∧ ∀ v : Rn m, ‖A v‖ ^ 2 ≤ hsNormSq A * ‖v‖ ^ 2
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the inequality ||A|| <= |A| (operator norm versus Hilbert-Schmidt norm) quoted in the Notation of the parent proof and used in its step 5 in the form |A v|^2 <= |A|^2 |v|^2, together with the continuity and boundedness of A -> |A|^2 that the parent needs to integrate |p_x - P|^2.

Notation. e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 for i in Fin m; these vectors form the standard orthonormal basis of R^m, so |e_i| = 1. For v in R^m, v_i denotes its i-th coordinate. By definition hsNormSq(A) = sum over i < m of |A e_i|^2. ||A|| is the operator norm of A : R^m ->L R^k.

1. Continuity. Fix i. The evaluation map A -> A e_i is linear in A and satisfies |A e_i - B e_i| = |(A - B) e_i| <= ||A - B|| |e_i| = ||A - B||, so it is continuous for the operator-norm topology. Composing with the continuous maps w -> |w| and t -> t^2 gives a continuous real function A -> |A e_i|^2. A finite sum of continuous real functions is continuous, so A -> sum_i |A e_i|^2 = hsNormSq(A) is continuous.
2. Nonnegativity. Every summand |A e_i|^2 is >= 0, hence hsNormSq(A) >= 0.
3. Upper bound by the operator norm. For each i, 0 <= |A e_i| <= ||A|| |e_i| = ||A||, so |A e_i|^2 <= ||A||^2. Summing over the m indices gives hsNormSq(A) <= sum_{i<m} ||A||^2 = m ||A||^2.
4. Coordinates. Every v in R^m satisfies v = sum_i v_i e_i, because the j-th coordinate of the right side is sum_i v_i delta_{ij} = v_j. For the Euclidean norm, |v|^2 = sum_i v_i^2 = sum_i |v_i|^2.
5. Bound on |A v|. By linearity of A and step 4, A v = sum_i v_i (A e_i). The triangle inequality and homogeneity of the norm give |A v| <= sum_i |v_i (A e_i)| = sum_i |v_i| |A e_i|.
6. Cauchy-Schwarz. For finite sums of real numbers, (sum_i a_i b_i)^2 <= (sum_i a_i^2)(sum_i b_i^2). With a_i = |v_i| and b_i = |A e_i| and step 4, (sum_i |v_i| |A e_i|)^2 <= (sum_i |v_i|^2)(sum_i |A e_i|^2) = |v|^2 hsNormSq(A).

subproblems.title: Rotated Lipschitz graph: closedness and slope bound relative to T_0
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, q a linear isometry of R^(n+l) onto itself, f : R^n -> R^l and eps >= 0, and suppose f is eps-Lipschitz on all of R^n (LipschitzWith (Real.toNNReal eps) f). Put Fhat := q(graphOver f R^n) = { q(graphPoint u (f u)) : u in R^n }, T_0 := rotatedPlane q = q(R^n x {0}), and let P be the orthogonal projection onto T_0 (T_0.starProjection). Then (a) Fhat is closed in R^(n+l), and (b) |(x - z) - P(x - z)| <= eps |x - z| for all x, z in Fhat.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (f : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε → LipschitzWith (Real.toNNReal ε) f → IsClosed (q '' graphOver f univ) ∧ ∀ x ∈ q '' graphOver f univ, ∀ z ∈ q '' graphOver f univ, ‖(x - z) - (rotatedPlane q).starProjection (x - z)‖ ≤ ε * ‖x - z‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 5 (the graph cone bound |Q(x - zeta)| <= eps |x - zeta| for x in Fhat, where Q = I - P, and the closedness of Fhat used to make Fhat Borel). Here it is proved for any two points x, z of Fhat.

Notation. graphPoint a b in R^(n+l) is the point whose first n coordinates are those of a in R^n and whose last l coordinates are those of b in R^l (Fin.append); its coordinates are indexed by Fin.castAdd l i (i < n) and Fin.natAdd n j (j < l). horizontalPlane n l is the span of the vectors e_(castAdd i) := EuclideanSpace.single (Fin.castAdd l i) 1, i < n, i.e. R^n x {0}. T_0 := rotatedPlane q = q(horizontalPlane n l), P := T_0.starProjection is the orthogonal projection onto T_0, and g(u) := graphPoint u (f u), so graphOver f R^n = range g and Fhat = q(range g).

1. Coordinate identities (compare coordinates separately at the indices castAdd i and natAdd j).
   (i) graphPoint a b - graphPoint a' b' = graphPoint (a - a') (b - b'), and graphPoint a b + graphPoint a' b' = graphPoint (a + a') (b + b').
   (ii) |graphPoint a b|^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2: split the sum of the squared coordinates over Fin (n + l) into the n indices castAdd i and the l indices natAdd j. Consequently |a| <= |graphPoint a b| (as |b|^2 >= 0) and |graphPoint 0 b| = |b| (both sides are nonnegative with equal squares).
   (iii) graphPoint a 0 = sum_{i<n} a_i e_(castAdd i). At an index castAdd j both sides equal a_j. At an index natAdd k the left side is 0, and each term on the right vanishes because castAdd i and natAdd k are different indices (their values are i < n and n + k >= n). Hence graphPoint a 0 is a linear combination of the spanning vectors of horizontalPlane n l and lies in it.
2. Lipschitz bound. Since eps >= 0, the real number underlying Real.toNNReal eps is eps. Hence the hypothesis LipschitzWith (Real.toNNReal eps) f gives |f u - f v| = dist(f u, f v) <= eps dist(u, v) = eps |u - v| for all u, v in R^n.
3. Closedness, part (a).
   (i) By 1(i) and 1(ii), |g u - g v|^2 = |graphPoint (u - v) (f u - f v)|^2 = |u - v|^2 + |f u - f v|^2.
   (ii) Hence |u - v| <= |g u - g v|, i.e. g is antilipschitz with constant 1.
   (iii) Also |g u - g v|^2 <= (|u - v| + |f u - f v|)^2 with both bases nonnegative, so |g u - g v| <= |u - v| + |f u - f v| <= (1 + eps)|u - v| by step 2. Thus g is Lipschitz, hence uniformly continuous.
   (iv) range g is closed: if g(u_k) -> w, then (g(u_k)) is Cauchy, so (u_k) is Cauchy by (ii); since R^n is complete, u_k -> u for some u, and by continuity g(u_k) -> g(u), so w = g(u) lies in range g. (This is the general fact that an antilipschitz, uniformly continuous map on a complete space has closed range.)
   (v) q is a linear isometry of R^(n+l) onto itself, hence a homeomorphism, and therefore maps the closed set range g = graphOver f R^n onto a closed set. So Fhat = q(graphOver f R^n) is closed.
4. The difference of two points of Fhat. Let x, z in Fhat, say x = q(g(u)) and z = q(g(v)) with u, v in R^n. By linearity of q and 1(i), x - z = q(g u - g v) = q(graphPoint (u - v) (f u - f v)). Put w := q(graphPoint (u - v) 0). By 1(iii), graphPoint (u - v) 0 lies in horizontalPlane n l, so w lies in its image T_0. By linearity of q and 1(i), (x - z) - w = q(graphPoint (u - v) (f u - f v) - graphPoint (u - v) 0) = q(graphPoint 0 (f u - f v)).
5. Distance to T_0. T_0 is a finite-dimensional, hence complete, subspace, and the orthogonal projection realises the distance to it: |y - P y| = dist(y, P y) = infDist(y, T_0) for every y. Since w lies in T_0, and q preserves norms, step 4 and 1(ii) give
   |(x - z) - P(x - z)| = infDist(x - z, T_0) <= dist(x - z, w) = |q(graphPoint 0 (f u - f v))| = |graphPoint 0 (f u - f v)| = |f u - f v|.
6. Conclusion, part (b). By step 2, then 1(ii) together with eps >= 0, then step 4 and the fact that q preserves norms:
   |f u - f v| <= eps |u - v| <= eps |graphPoint (u - v) (f u - f v)| = eps |q(graphPoint (u - v) (f u - f v))| = eps |x - z|.
   Combined with step 5, |(x - z) - P(x - z)| <= eps |x - z| for all x, z in Fhat. Together with step 3 this proves both assertions. QED

subproblems.title: Nearest point of spt V to a nearby point, and the empty ball around it
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, U a subset of R^(n+l), V a RectifiableVarifold n l U with weight mu = V.weight (so V.support = U ∩ spt mu, spt mu = Measure.support mu), rho real and zeta in R^(n+l); put d := infDist(zeta, V.support). If 0 ∈ V.support, the closed ball B_rho(0) ⊆ U, and |zeta| + d <= rho, then there is y in V.support with dist(y, zeta) = d, and the open ball of radius d about zeta has mu-measure 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (ρ : ℝ) (ζ : Amb n ℓ), (0 : Amb n ℓ) ∈ V.support → closedBall (0 : Amb n ℓ) ρ ⊆ U → ‖ζ‖ + infDist ζ V.support ≤ ρ → ∃ y ∈ V.support, dist y ζ = infDist ζ V.support ∧ V.weight (ball ζ (infDist ζ V.support)) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 2 (closest point), stated with exactly the hypotheses that step uses: 0 in spt V, B_rho(0) ⊆ U and |zeta| + d <= rho (in the parent, |zeta| + d <= 2 delta rho + delta rho = 3 delta rho <= rho). Neither openness of U nor d > 0 is needed.

Notation. mu := V.weight, S := spt mu = Measure.support mu, so V.support = U ∩ S by definition; d := infDist(zeta, V.support); B_rho(0) is the closed ball and ball(zeta, d) the open ball.

1. S is closed, because the support of a measure is closed. V.support = U ∩ S is a subset of S, and 0 ∈ V.support, so V.support and S are nonempty.
2. R^(n+l) is a proper metric space (closed bounded sets are compact), so the nonempty closed set S contains a point nearest to zeta: there is y ∈ S with dist(zeta, y) = infDist(zeta, S).
3. Since V.support ⊆ S and V.support is nonempty, infDist(zeta, S) <= infDist(zeta, V.support) = d. Hence dist(zeta, y) <= d.
4. By the triangle inequality, |y| = |zeta - (zeta - y)| <= |zeta| + |zeta - y| = |zeta| + dist(zeta, y) <= |zeta| + d <= rho. So y ∈ B_rho(0) ⊆ U, and therefore y ∈ U ∩ S = V.support.
5. As y ∈ V.support, d = infDist(zeta, V.support) <= dist(zeta, y). With step 3, dist(zeta, y) = d; by symmetry dist(y, zeta) = d. Moreover infDist(zeta, S) = dist(zeta, y) = d by step 2.
6. The open ball ball(zeta, d) does not meet S: if some x ∈ S had dist(x, zeta) < d, then infDist(zeta, S) <= dist(zeta, x) < d, contradicting step 5. Hence ball(zeta, d) is contained in the complement of S.
7. R^(n+l) is second countable, hence hereditarily Lindelöf, and in such a space the complement of the support of any measure is a null set: mu(complement of S) = 0. By monotonicity of mu, mu(ball(zeta, d)) <= mu(complement of S) = 0, so mu(ball(zeta, d)) = 0. (If d = 0 the open ball is empty, and the conclusion also holds.)
8. Steps 4, 5 and 7 give y ∈ V.support with dist(y, zeta) = infDist(zeta, V.support) and V.weight(ball(zeta, infDist(zeta, V.support))) = 0. QED

theorem lgc_support_closest_point : ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (ρ : ℝ) (ζ : Amb n ℓ), (0 : Amb n ℓ) ∈ V.support → closedBall (0 : Amb n ℓ) ρ ⊆ U → ‖ζ‖ + infDist ζ V.support ≤ ρ → ∃ y ∈ V.support, dist y ζ = infDist ζ V.support ∧ V.weight (ball ζ (infDist ζ V.support)) = 0 := by
  intro n ℓ U V ρ ζ h0 hB hsum
  set S := V.weight.support with hS
  have hSc : IsClosed S := Measure.isClosed_support
  have hVS : V.support ⊆ S := fun x hx => hx.2
  have hVne : V.support.Nonempty := ⟨0, h0⟩
  have hSne : S.Nonempty := hVne.mono hVS
  obtain ⟨y, hyS, hy⟩ := hSc.exists_infDist_eq_dist hSne ζ
  have hle : infDist ζ S ≤ infDist ζ V.support := infDist_le_infDist_of_subset hVS hVne
  have hyU : y ∈ U := by
    apply hB
    rw [mem_closedBall, dist_zero_right]
    have : ‖y‖ ≤ ‖ζ‖ + dist ζ y := by
      rw [dist_eq_norm]
      calc ‖y‖ = ‖ζ - (ζ - y)‖ := by rw [sub_sub_cancel]
        _ ≤ ‖ζ‖ + ‖ζ - y‖ := norm_sub_le _ _
    linarith
  have hyV : y ∈ V.support := ⟨hyU, hyS⟩
  have hge : infDist ζ V.support ≤ dist ζ y := infDist_le_dist_of_mem hyV
  have heq : dist ζ y = infDist ζ V.support := le_antisymm (hy ▸ hle) hge
  refine ⟨y, hyV, by rw [dist_comm]; exact heq, ?_⟩
  apply measure_mono_null _ (Measure.measure_compl_support (μ := V.weight))
  intro x hx hxS
  rw [mem_ball] at hx
  have : infDist ζ S ≤ dist ζ x := infDist_le_dist_of_mem hxS
  rw [dist_comm] at hx
  linarith

subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers and mu a measure on R^(n+l). Let p : R^(n+l) -> L(R^(n+l)) be a mu-a.e. strongly measurable field of continuous linear maps with operator norm ||p(x)|| <= 1 for all x. Let zeta, y be points of R^(n+l), s > 0, omega > 0 and c real. Write B_r(w) for closed balls, g(x) := |(x - zeta) - p(x)(x - zeta)|^2, and I := the Bochner integral of g over B_{3s}(zeta) with respect to mu. Assume: (1) mu(B_s(zeta)) = 0; (2) mu(B_{3s}(zeta)) < infinity; (3) dist(y, zeta) <= 2s; (4) ENNReal.ofReal(omega s^n / 2) <= mu(B_s(y)); (5) c <= omega/(4 * 3^n); (6) the annular monotonicity inequality ((3s)^n)^(-1) mu(B_{3s}(zeta)) <= e^2 ((s^n)^(-1) mu(B_s(zeta))) + c + e^2 J, where J := the Bochner integral over B_{3s}(zeta) minus B_s(zeta) of g(x)/|x - zeta|^(n+2) dmu and the ball masses are real numbers (toReal). Then s^(n+2) <= (4 * 3^n * e^2 / omega) * I.

Source: parent proof, steps 3-4 (monotonicity at zeta on the annulus B_{3s}(zeta) minus B_s(zeta), with the empty ball B_s(zeta), and the lower bound via the nearby support point y), with the density inputs turned into explicit hypotheses.

Context only (not used in the argument). In the parent's application mu = V.weight, p = V.tangentProj, omega = unitBallVolume n and c = C_0 delta; hypothesis (6) is item (iii) of the sibling density_monotonicity at the centre zeta with radii s <= 3s, hypothesis (4) is item (ii) at y, and (5) holds because C_0 delta <= 3^-n omega_n/4. The proof below uses only s > 0, omega > 0, the a.e. strong measurability of p, ||p(x)|| <= 1 and hypotheses (1)-(6).

Notation. B := B_{3s}(zeta) (closed ball), A := B minus B_s(zeta) (a measurable set), g(x) := |(x - zeta) - p(x)(x - zeta)|^2, I := integral over B of g dmu, J := integral over A of g(x)/|x - zeta|^(n+2) dmu. All integrals are Bochner integrals.

1. Measurability. The map x -> x - zeta is continuous, and the evaluation (L, v) -> L v is jointly continuous on L(R^(n+l)) x R^(n+l). Hence x -> p(x)(x - zeta), a continuous function of the a.e. strongly measurable p and the continuous x -> x - zeta, is mu-a.e. strongly measurable. Therefore x -> (x - zeta) - p(x)(x - zeta) and its squared norm g are mu-a.e. strongly measurable.
2. Integrability. For x ∈ B, |x - zeta| <= 3s, so |(x - zeta) - p(x)(x - zeta)| <= |x - zeta| + ||p(x)|| |x - zeta| <= 3s + 3s = 6s and 0 <= g(x) <= 36 s^2. A bounded a.e. strongly measurable function is integrable on a set of finite measure; by (2), mu(B) < infinity, so g is mu-integrable on B, and hence on A ⊆ B.
3. Annulus comparison. For x ∈ A, x is not in B_s(zeta), so |x - zeta| > s > 0, hence |x - zeta|^(n+2) >= s^(n+2) > 0 and 0 <= g(x)/|x - zeta|^(n+2) <= (s^(n+2))^(-1) g(x).
   (i) The function (s^(n+2))^(-1) g is integrable on A (step 2) and g/|x - zeta|^(n+2) is nonnegative. For the Bochner integral, a nonnegative function dominated a.e. by an integrable function has integral at most the integral of that function (no integrability of the smaller function is needed). So J <= integral over A of (s^(n+2))^(-1) g dmu = (s^(n+2))^(-1) * integral over A of g dmu.
   (ii) Since g >= 0 is integrable on B ⊇ A, the integral of g over A is at most the integral of g over B, which is I.
   (iii) Hence J <= (s^(n+2))^(-1) I.
4. Mass lower bound. B_s(y) ⊆ B: for x ∈ B_s(y), dist(x, zeta) <= dist(x, y) + dist(y, zeta) <= s + 2s = 3s by (3). By (4) and monotonicity of mu, ENNReal.ofReal(omega s^n/2) <= mu(B_s(y)) <= mu(B), and mu(B) < infinity by (2). Converting to real numbers, omega s^n/2 <= mu(B).toReal.
5. Using (6). By (1), mu(B_s(zeta)).toReal = 0, so the first term on the right of (6) vanishes and (6) reads ((3s)^n)^(-1) mu(B).toReal <= c + e^2 J. Since ((3s)^n)^(-1) (omega s^n/2) = omega/(2 * 3^n) and ((3s)^n)^(-1) > 0, step 4 gives omega/(2 * 3^n) <= ((3s)^n)^(-1) mu(B).toReal. Using step 3(iii) multiplied by e^2 >= 0:
   omega/(2 * 3^n) <= c + e^2 J <= c + e^2 (s^(n+2))^(-1) I.
6. Absorbing c. By (5), c <= omega/(4 * 3^n), and omega/(2 * 3^n) = omega/(4 * 3^n) + omega/(4 * 3^n). So step 5 gives omega/(4 * 3^n) <= e^2 (s^(n+2))^(-1) I. Multiplying both sides by the positive number 4 * 3^n * s^(n+2)/omega gives s^(n+2) <= (4 * 3^n * e^2/omega) * I, which is the claim. QED

subproblems.title: Upper bound for the normal-part integral by slope, mass off the graph, and tilt
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers and mu a measure on R^(n+l). Let p : R^(n+l) -> L(R^(n+l)) be a mu-a.e. strongly measurable field of continuous linear maps with ||p(x)|| <= 1 for all x. Let T be a linear subspace of R^(n+l) with orthogonal projection P = T.starProjection, F a measurable subset of R^(n+l), zeta in R^(n+l), s > 0 and eps real. Write B := B_{3s}(zeta) (closed ball), and assume mu(B) < infinity and |(x - zeta) - P(x - zeta)| <= eps |x - zeta| for every x in F. Then the Bochner integral over B of |(x - zeta) - p(x)(x - zeta)|^2 dmu is at most 18 s^2 [ eps^2 mu(B) + mu(B minus F) + the Bochner integral over B of hsNormSq(p(x) - P) dmu ], with the masses taken as real numbers (toReal).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (p : Amb n ℓ → (Amb n ℓ →L[ℝ] Amb n ℓ)) (T : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ)) (F : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (ζ : Amb n ℓ) (s ε : ℝ), 0 < s → AEStronglyMeasurable p μ → (∀ x, ‖p x‖ ≤ 1) → MeasurableSet F → μ (closedBall ζ (3 * s)) ≠ ⊤ → (∀ x ∈ F, ‖(x - ζ) - T.starProjection (x - ζ)‖ ≤ ε * ‖x - ζ‖) → ∫ x in closedBall ζ (3 * s), ‖(x - ζ) - p x (x - ζ)‖ ^ 2 ∂μ ≤ 18 * s ^ 2 * (ε ^ 2 * (μ (closedBall ζ (3 * s))).toReal + (μ (closedBall ζ (3 * s) \ F)).toReal + ∫ x in closedBall ζ (3 * s), hsNormSq (p x - T.starProjection) ∂μ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 5: the splitting p_x^perp = Q + (P - p_x), the graph cone bound on Fhat (here replaced by the slope hypothesis on the measurable set F), the trivial bound off F, and integration over B_{3s}(zeta). Uses the sibling child hs_norm_bounds with m = k = n + l: A -> hsNormSq(A) is continuous, and 0 <= hsNormSq(A) <= (n + l)||A||^2 and |A v|^2 <= hsNormSq(A)|v|^2 for every linear map A of R^(n+l) and every v.

Notation. B := B_{3s}(zeta) (closed ball, measurable, mu(B) < infinity by hypothesis), P := T.starProjection (orthogonal projection onto T; T is finite-dimensional, hence complete, so P exists and ||P|| <= 1), h(x) := hsNormSq(p(x) - P), and 1_{F^c} is the indicator function of the complement F^c of F (equal to 1 off F and 0 on F). All integrals are Bochner integrals.

1. Integrability of the right-hand integrands.
   (i) x -> p(x) - P is a.e. strongly measurable (difference of an a.e. strongly measurable function and a constant), and hsNormSq is continuous (hs_norm_bounds), so h is a.e. strongly measurable.
   (ii) ||p(x) - P|| <= ||p(x)|| + ||P|| <= 1 + 1 = 2, so 0 <= h(x) <= (n + l)||p(x) - P||^2 <= 4(n + l) for every x (hs_norm_bounds).
   (iii) A bounded a.e. strongly measurable function is integrable on a set of finite measure, so h is integrable on B. The constant eps^2 is integrable on B, and so is 1_{F^c}, the indicator of the measurable set F^c applied to the integrable constant 1.
2. Pointwise splitting. Fix x ∈ B and put v := x - zeta, so |v| <= 3s. Since v - p(x)v = (v - Pv) + (-(p(x) - P)v), the triangle inequality gives |v - p(x)v| <= |v - Pv| + |(p(x) - P)v|. Both sides are nonnegative, so squaring and using (a + b)^2 <= 2a^2 + 2b^2 (equivalent to (a - b)^2 >= 0) gives
   |v - p(x)v|^2 <= 2|v - Pv|^2 + 2|(p(x) - P)v|^2.
   By hs_norm_bounds, |(p(x) - P)v|^2 <= h(x)|v|^2 <= 9 s^2 h(x), using h(x) >= 0.
3. The term |v - Pv|.
   (i) If x ∈ F, the slope hypothesis gives 0 <= |v - Pv| <= eps|v|; squaring (0 <= a <= b implies a^2 <= b^2) gives |v - Pv|^2 <= eps^2 |v|^2 <= 9 eps^2 s^2. No sign condition on eps is needed.
   (ii) If x ∉ F, then |v - Pv| = dist(v, Pv) = infDist(v, T) <= dist(v, 0) = |v|, because the orthogonal projection realises the distance to T and 0 ∈ T. So |v - Pv|^2 <= |v|^2 <= 9 s^2.
4. Pointwise bound. In case (i), 1_{F^c}(x) = 0 and |v - p(x)v|^2 <= 18 eps^2 s^2 + 18 s^2 h(x) = 18 s^2 (eps^2 + 1_{F^c}(x) + h(x)). In case (ii), 1_{F^c}(x) = 1 and |v - p(x)v|^2 <= 18 s^2 + 18 s^2 h(x) <= 18 s^2 (eps^2 + 1 + h(x)) = 18 s^2 (eps^2 + 1_{F^c}(x) + h(x)), since eps^2 >= 0. So for every x ∈ B:
   |(x - zeta) - p(x)(x - zeta)|^2 <= 18 s^2 (eps^2 + 1_{F^c}(x) + h(x)).
